facts.text: Sorel-Tracy formed in March 2000 from a voluntary merger of Sorel and Tracy, on opposite shores of the Richelieu River.
facts.evidence: The city is the result of a voluntary merger in March 2000 between two former municipalities, Sorel and Tracy, which developed on opposite shores of the Richelieu River

meta.descriptor: an industrial city where the Richelieu River meets the St. Lawrence
meta.fact: home to Rio Tinto Fer et Titane's metallurgical complex, which employs 1,800 people

overview: Sorel-Tracy had 35,165 residents in the 2021 Census, living in 17,070 occupied dwellings on 57.28 square kilometres. The city straddles the Richelieu River, joining the former towns of Sorel and Tracy, so customers often think of themselves as belonging to one side or the other.

Heavy industry, led by a large Rio Tinto metallurgical complex, shapes local jobs and incomes, and changes at that plant ripple through household spending. Local businesses compete for a stable, French-speaking population that values long relationships and nearby service.
